SMTO-EXE-0194 — SMTO can't find the PDF file

GUID: 90ffd98d-37f4-5473-80f9-5c081f7d167b
Slug: pdf-file-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • SMTO looked for the PDF on the computer running the Gateway (the helper program that works with files there), but there is no file at that location. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer that runs the Gateway, find the PDF and copy its full location, including the folder and the file name ending in .pdf. SMTO looks for the file on the Gateway's computer, which may not be the computer you are using.
  2. Ask SMTO again using that full location, checking spelling, spaces and capital letters. A small difference in the name or folder points to a file that doesn't exist.
  3. If the PDF is on your own computer and you only need SMTO to read it, use Add files to conversation and ask again. Adding the file lets SMTO make its own copy to read on the Gateway.
  4. If the file was moved, renamed or deleted after SMTO first saw it, put it back or give SMTO its new location. SMTO can't use a location that no longer holds the file.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the PDF and finishes the step.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the full file location and which Gateway you used, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PDF processing raised FileNotFoundError or the File layer reported a missing local resource on the selected Gateway.

What this means

  • PDF processing caught FileNotFoundError or the File layer reported a missing local resource. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • PDF processing caught FileNotFoundError or the File layer reported a missing local resource.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the exact requested local or run-artifact input; another Gateway's path is not interchangeable.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the exact path exists on the selected Gateway host (paths resolve relative to the task's working directory, not the user's browser machine), or for read operations use an authorized conversation attachment; artifact-workspace:// paths resolve only within the current run.
  • Materialize the input on the selected Gateway and use its exact local or artifact-workspace path.

Retry and execution caution

  • Materialize the input on the selected Gateway and use its exact local or artifact-workspace path.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended file is materialized and resolves on the selected Gateway before processing.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
